Messages.Author: Christoph Scherer
Messages.Body:
> Can you make directed actions against yourself?
> Like diablerize one of your own vamps...
>
> bobby_doc

If you mak a D-action against yourself, it is no longer considered directed
(and your predator and prey can attempt to block it).

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
"Christoph Scherer" <csch...@frankfurt.fcb.com> wrote:
> > Can you make directed actions against yourself?
> > Like diablerize one of your own vamps...
>

> If you mak a D-action against yourself, it is no longer considered
> directed (and your predator and prey can attempt to block it).

Correct. An action is not directed until the target is declared.
If the target is another Methuselah (or something she controls),
then the action is directed. If not, it is undirected. [6.2.2]

Diablerizing one of your own is undirected. [6.5.4]
Rescuing someone else's vampire is directed. [6.5.3]

Did you even bother to read the rule quoted?
WTF!

"6.5.4. Diablerize a Vampire in Torpor
To have one vampire diablerize another vampire in torpor,
announce the action and tap the acting vampire. If the action
is successful, the victim is diablerized (see below). If the action
is blocked, the acting vampire and the blocking minion enter
combat as normal. This action has a default +1 stealth if the
acting vampire and the vampire in torpor have the same
controller; otherwise, it is simply a directed action. Allies
cannot take this action."

> > Rescuing someone else's vampire is directed. [6.5.3]
> is the rescued vampire forced to pay blood ?

Yes, if it is announced as such when the action is announced.

> can he decide not to pay and stay in torpor (eg fame) ?

No.

The controller of the acting minion makes all decisions
about the action. The only way for the vampire to stay
in torpor is if its controller (or someone else) blocks.
The acting minion's controller may choose to have the
rescuee pay any or all of the cost of the rescue.
Who will pay what part of the cost is announced when
the action is announced.

Carpe Noctem.
